The targeted change shifts 0.02 weight from static nearness to positive approach rate. This should better separate genuinely approaching hazards from merely close objects, improving rankings while addressing both diagnostics in the desired direction: fewer false-clears for approaching objects and fewer false-blocks caused by static nearness. The reliability correction remains small and corroboration-gated, so weak quality cannot broadly suppress strong evidence.

        + 0.15 * f["path_intrusion"]

                  + f["observation_quality"] - 1.0) * min(a, e))

The base coefficients still sum to 1.0, preserving calibration and the finite `[0, 1]` bound for normalized inputs. Clamping only the two signed motion observations prevents receding motion from becoming artificial negative risk. The historical results make this conservative motion-sensitive rebalancing preferable to adding nonlinear complexity, but only the frozen deterministic evaluator can establish whether it improves the synthetic benchmark; it is not evidence of real-world headroom or safety.
